sheet-1-1.description: The main part of sheet 1 is the lower half of the sheet below the key map and index; it is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and shows the residential district east of the town centre along Atco Avenue. Atco Avenue crosses the part from left to right with 2nd Street, 3rd Street and 4th Street crossing it; below Atco Avenue the part takes in Auburn Avenue and, at the bottom left, Bartram Avenue, between the left edge and 3rd Street. 2nd Street jogs at Atco Avenue, the section north of it lying west of the section south of it. The blocks are large and lightly built: frame dwellings with coops, sheds and private garages, some lots still empty, and block 97 between 3rd and 4th Streets crossed by a narrow alley. The First Presbyterian Church, a frame building with steam heat and electric lighting, stands at the left edge on the north side of Atco Avenue. A large compass rose is drawn in block 15 north of Atco Avenue. The lower right quarter of the sheet is a separate part, cut off by a heavy line that follows 3rd Street below Auburn Avenue and 4th Street, and shows Atco Avenue further east; the main part reaches only the west half of 3rd Street there. The upper half of the sheet, with the key map at 1000 feet to an inch, the legend, the water and fire department notes and the index of specials, is left out of the mask.
notes: 2nd Street jogs at Atco Avenue; OpenStreetMap has two junctions there, both used.
3rd Street / Auburn Avenue was left out of the fit: the junction straddles the heavy line dividing the two parts and sat 4.4 m off.
1st Presbyn Church (First Presbyterian Church) on Atco Avenue at the left edge.

Map, 100 ft. Top half is the key map (1000 ft), index, legend and title: masked out. Two parts: part 1 Atco Av, Auburn Av, Bartram Av with 2nd, 3rd, 4th Sts (2nd St jogs at Atco Av); part 2 (lower right, behind a heavy line) Atco Av from 4th to 5th St, the continuation east. Part 1: 6 points, 3rd St/Auburn Av excluded (straddles the part divider, 4.4 m off); mask cut at the east edge of 4th St. Part 2: helmert from 4th St/Atco and 5th St/Atco only (low confidence; scale and rotation agree with the atlas).

sheet-1-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 1 is the lower right quarter of the sheet, set off by a heavy line along its top and left side, and drawn at 100 feet to an inch in the same orientation as the main part. It continues Atco Avenue eastward from 4th Street, along whose centre the dividing line runs, to 5th Street and a little beyond, so that it lies east of the main part on the ground rather than below it. Block 16 lies north of Atco Avenue between 4th and 5th Streets and block 104 south of it, with blocks 17 and 19 beyond 5th Street. The blocks are deep and thinly built: frame dwellings, long poultry coops, a building for the storage of hay and feed at the north-east corner of block 16, and a range of greenhouses with a heater room and coal pile on the south side of Atco Avenue near 4th Street. A narrow alley crosses block 104. The edges of the part marked no exposure have nothing drawn beyond them. The sheet's scale bar and copyright line sit in the main part to the left.
notes: Placed from two junctions on Atco Avenue only (4th and 5th Streets), so the placement is a similarity (helmert) fit; its scale and rotation (3.97 px/ft, 30.0 degrees) agree with the other sheets.
Green houses on Atco Avenue near 4th Street.

Part 1: 6 points, 3rd St/Auburn Av excluded (straddles the part divider, 4.4 m off); mask cut at the east edge of 4th St. Part 2: helmert from 4th St/Atco and 5th St/Atco only (low confidence; scale and rotation agree with the atlas).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the centre of Atco in Waterford Township, Camden County, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It runs from Camilla Avenue at the top to Bartram Avenue at the bottom and from West Front Street on the left edge to just beyond Front Street on the right, with Bellevue, Almira, Atco and Auburn Avenues crossing the sheet between them. The West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Pennsylvania Railroad) runs down the middle of the sheet in a wide right-of-way between Atlantic Avenue on its west side and Raritan Avenue on its east side; Raritan Avenue leaves the tracks below Atco Avenue and runs off diagonally to the south-east. The Atco station stands beside the tracks north of Atco Avenue, with the post office just south of the crossing. Atco Avenue is the business street: a hall with stores, a storage garage and small shops line it east of the railroad, and the Atco National Bank stands on West Front Street. Church Street, which jogs at Atco Avenue, divides the blocks east of the railroad. In the lower left corner, in the angle between Auburn Avenue and the curving Williamstown and Delaware River branch, is the broom factory of the Union Novelty Manufacturing Company, with its manufacturing building, storage houses and sheds. The rest of the sheet is frame dwellings on large lots, many with coops and sheds, and several blocks at the edges are still mostly vacant. Front Street on the right is drawn only north of Bellevue Avenue and south of Auburn Avenue.
notes: Camilla Avenue is spelled Camila Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
West Front is Front Street today; Atlantic Avenue is West Atlantic Avenue.
Front (east of Church) is Gardens Avenue north of Bellevue Avenue and 1st Street south of Auburn Avenue today; 1st Street was left out of the fit because its junctions sat 3.6 to 4 m off.
The railroad is labelled both Penn. R.R. and W. J. & S. R. R. (West Jersey and Seashore Railroad); OpenStreetMap names the line the Atlantic City Line.
Union Novelty Mfg. Co., brooms manufacturer, in the lower left corner; the W. & D. R. R. siding curves through it.

Map, 100 ft, one part. Town centre: Camilla, Bellevue, Almira, Atco, Auburn, Bartram Avs; W. Front, Atlantic Av, Raritan Av, Church, Front (east); West Jersey & Seashore RR (Penna RR) with Atco station; Union Novelty Mfg Co broom works. Printed east Front is Gardens Avenue (north) and 1st Street (south) today; 1st Street left out (junctions 3.6-4 m off, RMSE 1.7 -> 1.0 m without it). Camilla Av is Camila Avenue in OSM.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the west end of Atco, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. White Horse Pike crosses it diagonally from the top left to the bottom, meeting Atco Avenue near the middle of the sheet; Granger Avenue and an unnamed street run parallel to the Pike on its west side, and Cooper Road, marked as not opened, leaves the Pike towards the north-east. On the right the sheet reaches West 2nd Street and West Front Street, with Almira, Atco and Auburn Avenues crossing them, and joins sheet 2 along West Front. The Williamstown and Delaware River Railroad crosses the lower part of the sheet from left to right. Most of the sheet is open land in large lots: block 57 north of Atco Avenue is almost empty, and the large block 23 south-west of the Pike has only a few dwellings. Buildings are mostly frame dwellings with poultry houses, coops and sheds, a greenhouse with its heater room and pump house east of the Pike, and long poultry houses at the top left. Along the Pike near Atco Avenue are two garages: one for 14 cars on the west side of the Pike, and one of concrete block for 5 cars with gasoline tanks on its east side south of Atco Avenue. Institutions are the Atco M.E. Church on Atco Avenue at West 2nd Street, a church on the Pike south of Atco Avenue, and the public school on West Front Street between Atco and Auburn Avenues. The Texas Company oil tanks stand beside the railroad on Auburn Avenue at the Pike.
notes: West 2nd Street is Carl Hasselhan Drive today; West Front is Front Street.
Cooper Road is marked not opened; the modern Cooper Road runs close to the drawn line but was left out of the fit.
The W. & D. R. R. (Williamstown and Delaware River Railroad) crossing the lower part of the sheet is not in OpenStreetMap.
The narrow lane between blocks 62 and 63 is Schoolhouse Lane today; it was left out of the fit.

Map, 100 ft, one part. West end: White Horse Pike, Granger Av, Cooper Rd (not opened), Atco, Almira, Auburn Avs, W. 2nd St, W. Front; Williamstown & Delaware River RR (W.&D.R.R., gone); public school, Atco M.E. church. W. 2nd St is Carl Hasselhan Drive; Cooper Rd (not opened) and Schoolhouse Lane (alley) left out.
